preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in stdin.split()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each p_i in the input is an integer between 1 and n (inclusive), where n is the number of students.
The input consists of exactly two lines: the first line contains n, and the second line contains n integers p_1, ..., p_n.
The first line of input is the integer n, which matches the number of integers in the second line.

postconditions.expression: stdout == ' '.join(str(find_two_holes(a, p)) for a in range(1, n + 1)) + ' '
postconditions.description: For each student a from 1 to n, the output contains the student who would receive two holes if a was the first student caught, separated by spaces. The function find_two_holes(a, p) returns the student with two holes when starting from student a, where p is the list of p_i values (1-indexed).

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= find_two_holes(a, p) <= n for a in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: The output for each student a is a valid student number between 1 and n (inclusive).
